inherent_strain.source: Demonstration eigenstrain tensor; not a calibrated machine or material

material.note: a body loaded only by an eigenstrain has a displacement field that does not depend on the modulus; it sets the stresses

cut.from_x_measured_from: the part's own minimum x (its fixed end), not the build frame origin
cut.rule: every element beyond from_x whose z extent crosses the kerf band is removed; what lies before it keeps the part on the plate

results.tip_definition: max u_z over the nodes at the free end (largest x), +z up
results.stress_field_definition: element mean of eight Gauss-point von Mises values, not a Gauss-point maximum
results.equilibrium_error_definition: recovered linear free residual norm / (applied nodal load norm + individual constrained reaction norm + assembled free RHS norm including eigenstrain); absolute residual in N if scale is zero
results.max_displacement_definition: largest total displacement over the nodes of the part (supports excluded), from the plate's reference

scope.statement: inherent-strain process simulation: the strain is a declared process input, not a material property. Predictive use requires calibration for the relevant process and geometry; inspect the recorded provenance, which may be inferred demonstration values
scope.method: layer-by-layer activation, each layer stress-free on the deformed part, then its eigenstrain, then equilibrium
not_modelled: the thermal history and the melt pool
support structures other than the geometry itself
residual stress from the cutting process
scope.use: compare strategies, orientations and geometries; a number becomes a claim only against a measurement under a protocol written before the run
